stories.title: Nasdaq falls 1.48% as chips give back Monday's surge; Dow ends above 50,000
stories.body: The S&P 500 fell 36.07 points (0.50%) to 7,201.10 and the Nasdaq Composite 356.02 points (1.48%) to 23,733.54, while the Dow rose 424.46 points (0.86%) to 50,019.77 and the Russell 2000 gained 0.57%. AP said AI stocks dragged the market as Monday's surge fizzled, on worries that AI-related stock prices had 'shot too high'; Anthropic fell below its $83 IPO price. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.90% from 4.92% late Monday.
stories.why: Monday's +4.73% S&P 500 day was partly retraced, with the Dow and Nasdaq moving in opposite directions. Completed 1-hour closes on SPY and QQQ show whether that split carries into Wednesday's data-heavy session.

stories.title: Apple and Microsoft rise while Amazon, Meta and Alphabet slip
stories.body: At the 4:00 PM close Apple was at $354.19 (+1.46%) and Microsoft at $496.47 (+0.81%), while Amazon ended at $252.31 (−1.21%), Meta at $590.23 (−1.23%) and Alphabet's GOOG at $276.64 (−1.03%). Today's sources gave no company-specific reason for these moves; Yahoo Finance's live blog carried a report that Microsoft declared a 'code red' after a Nov. 12–13 outage.
stories.why: Megacaps split from chip stocks, holding the S&P 500's loss to half a percent. Their hourly closes relative to Monday's wide ranges show whether money is rotating within tech rather than leaving it.

stories.title: Chip stocks slide: Micron −11%, AMD −9% as the AI trade comes under renewed pressure
stories.body: Micron ended at $629.79 (−11.01%), AMD at $413.24 (−8.87%), Intel at $54.90 (−7.98%) and Broadcom at $301.23 (−3.93%), giving back part of Monday's rally. Yahoo Finance said chip stocks fell 'as the overall AI trade came under renewed pressure', with Micron and SK Hynix down more than 10%. FinanceFeeds noted an AMD registration filed Nov. 23 covering the resale of about 336.9 million shares, including up to 160 million each tied to OpenAI and Meta warrants. Investrade noted BNP cut Micron to Neutral with a $775 target, from $1,700.
stories.why: Double-digit swings in both directions on consecutive days keep implied volatility and option premiums in chip names elevated; completed 1-hour closes filter the noise of intrahour reversals.

stories.title: Energy and bank shares help lift the Dow
stories.body: Chevron ended at $208.81 (+1.28%), Exxon at $158.40 (+0.96%), Bank of America at $48.58 (+0.91%) and JPMorgan at $317.25 (+0.19%) as the Dow rose 0.86%. WTI settled at $82.05 (+2.35%) and Brent at $91.40 (+2.27%) (Investrade), rebounding from Monday's three-month low as traders weighed continued ship attacks near the Strait of Hormuz (Rallies). Yahoo Finance carried a report that US banks' paper bond losses jumped nearly 50% in the third quarter.
stories.why: Banks and energy are moving on rates and oil rather than on the AI trade, which shows up as low correlation with QQQ on the hourly chart.

stories.title: Nvidia falls 5.8% a day after its 31% Huang-return surge
stories.body: Nvidia ended at $155.48 (−5.80%) after closing Monday at $165.05 (+31.48%), its biggest gain in more than two decades, when the board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. The Motley Fool pointed to profit-taking and to Reuters' report that lawmakers from both parties sharply criticized the rehiring; Reuters also said Huang and the company face state and federal probes and reviews, including from the FBI, the Justice Department and the SEC. Yahoo Finance said Sen. Ruben Gallego expects Senate Banking testimony on Dec. 3.
stories.why: Two sessions with ranges above 9% leave the stock far from its moving averages; with governance and probe headlines still unfolding, completed 1-hour closes matter more than headline prints.

stories.title: Gold and silver slide as Fed-hike bets firm before PCE
stories.body: GLD ended at $325.48 (−2.26%) and SLV at $36.84 (−5.32%). Kitco said gold struggled to extend Monday's rebound as expectations of more Fed rate increases pressured silver, and Yahoo Finance said Wednesday's PCE report could 'cement the Fed's position of raising rates in a few weeks.' December gold futures settled at $3,561.90 (−2.45%) and December silver at $40.78 (−5.54%) (Investrade).
stories.why: Metals ETFs are trading on rate expectations into a scheduled 8:30 AM ET data release, a known overnight gap risk; the next completed hourly candle after the release shows how the market took it.

stories.title: Hormuz ship attacks and a tanker-cyberattack probe keep oil risk in view
stories.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a container ship was targeted near the Strait of Hormuz, and UKMTO said three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles while sailing east through the strait on Monday, with all crew accounted for (Rallies). The Wall Street Journal reported the US is investigating whether Iran was involved in cyberattacks on as many as 50 energy tankers; a Trump administration official said no evidence of Iranian involvement had been found (Cornerstone Futures). WTI settled at $82.05 (+2.35%) (Investrade); OPEC+ ministers meet Sunday, Nov. 29. USO ended at $135.55 (+1.64%) and Occidental at $53.38 (+1.29%).
stories.why: Headline-driven oil can gap between sessions, and the Thanksgiving break adds a day without US trading; USO and OXY hourly closes show whether the market prices the incidents as supply risk.

stories.title: VIX holds in the high 20s as stocks split
stories.body: The VIX was at 27.05 (+1.62%) around 3:29 PM ET, per Yahoo Finance, after a late-morning reading of 28.87 (FinanceFeeds); it closed Monday at 26.62 (−25.84%). Saxo said Monday's rally flattened the volatility curve: all six VIX tenors sat between 25.47 and 27.76, the VIX3M/VIX ratio rose to 0.96 and the SKEW index was 140.37.
stories.why: A VIX in the high 20s keeps option premiums and expected moves well above normal, and a flat curve means near-dated protection is priced about the same as longer-dated.

stories.title: 5-year auction tails slightly as December hike odds hold near 95%
stories.body: The Treasury sold $70 billion of 5-year notes at a 4.719% high yield, a 0.3 bp tail to the 4.716% when-issued level, with a 2.37 bid-to-cover (investingLive); TheStreet Pro said the 54.3% indirect share was the lowest since March 2020. The 10-year yield eased to 4.90% from 4.92% late Monday (AP). Yahoo Finance said traders priced a 95% chance of a 25 bp Fed hike in December and 5% odds of 50 bp. A $44 billion 7-year sale follows Wednesday.
stories.why: Rate-hike pricing is the macro backdrop for the tech pullback; auction results and Wednesday's PCE can move yields and index ETFs within a single hourly candle.

stories.title: Asia rallies on Huang's return while Europe slips on chip and mining losses
stories.body: Trading Economics reported Japan's Nikkei 225 up 3.91% to 58,645 in a post-holiday session and Korea's KOSPI up 6.32% to 5,006 on renewed AI optimism, while the Shanghai Composite rose 0.27%; 24/7 Wall St. said the Hang Seng closed down 0.82%. In Europe the DAX fell 1.29% to 25,012 as Infineon dropped about 9%, and the FTSE 100 edged lower as miners led declines; the CAC 40 edged up 0.2%, helped by Sanofi's $41 billion Insmed deal.
stories.why: Overseas chip suppliers moved with Monday's US rally before Tuesday's US pullback, so overnight markets are lagging the US tape this week.

stories.title: Consumer confidence jumps to 103.3 in November
stories.body: The Conference Board's consumer confidence index rose 11.4 points to 103.3 in November from 91.9 in October, well above the 92.1 consensus cited by The Weekend Spread. The Present Situation Index rose to 132.8 and the Expectations Index to 83.6. The Rio Times reported that respondents saying jobs are 'plentiful' rose to 30.8% from 26.2%, and 12-month inflation expectations were 5.7%.
stories.why: A strong data surprise adds to the case the Fed is already pricing for a December hike; Wednesday's PCE release is the next scheduled data risk.

stories.title: Options price about a 2% S&P 500 move into Friday; chip implied volatility stays high
stories.body: Saxo's options brief said S&P 500 options priced about 151.80 points (2.09%) of movement into the Nov. 27 expiry, down from 271.80 in its prior edition, and that Monday's 7,237.17 close used 120% of the prior week's implied range. At Monday's close, implied-volatility rank was 75.5 for Nvidia and 77.0 for the semiconductor fund, against a median single-name rank of 39.2. Longbridge counted 11,004,818 Nvidia options traded Monday, 60% of them calls.
stories.why: Expected-move pricing shows how wide a range the options market allows through the holiday-shortened week; it is reported market data, not a signal.

stories.title: Ahead: PCE, GDP and claims at 8:30 AM Wednesday, then Thanksgiving
stories.body: Wednesday at 8:30 AM ET brings October PCE (core forecast +0.3% m/m, the same as the prior month), the second estimate of Q3 GDP (forecast 3.5% vs 3.4% initially) and weekly jobless claims (forecast 201,000), per Gotrade, plus October durable goods. The Treasury sells $44 billion of 7-year notes and the Fed's Beige Book is due at 2:00 PM ET. Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close at 1:00 PM ET Friday. OPEC+ meets Nov. 29, Huang faces House committees Dec. 1, and Broadcom reports Dec. 9 after the close.
stories.why: A heavy data morning before a holiday break means fewer completed hourly candles and possible gaps around Thursday's closure and Friday's early close.
